Accord

/uh-KORD/ - rhymes with reward · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Accord means a formal agreement between parties.

The two rival taxi companies signed an accord that splits the airport queue by odd and even days.

Worked Example

In 1874 twenty-two nations signed a postal accord: one flat rate, one set of rules, so a letter posted in Lisbon could reach Oslo without a dozen separate arrangements along the way.

Accord is more formal than a mere understanding and lighter than a treaty — it names a negotiated agreement between parties who stay independent, and it usually closes a stretch of quarreling.

How Accord Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

pact

pact: a tight, sometimes secret agreement among few parties — an accord is fuller and more public

settlement

settlement: an agreement that closes one specific dispute, often legal

Antonyms

dispute

dispute: an open disagreement still running

rift

rift: a break between parties, agreement gone

How Strong Is It? — understanding → accord → treaty

understanding vs. accord

understanding vs. accord: An understanding is the quiet, unwritten version — nothing signed, nothing binding, well short of an accord.

treaty vs. accord

treaty vs. accord: A treaty goes further than an accord — ratified by governments and enforceable as law, not just signed intent.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ac-

Prefix — ac-: to, toward (a form of ad-)

Root — cord-

Root — cord-: heart

Put it together

Put it together: Ac- (to, toward) + cord- (heart) = heart to heart. Latin accordare meant to bring two hearts into agreement, and an accord is exactly that — two sides whose wills now beat together on paper. Its neighbor in this unit, concord, grows from the same heart-root: the accord is signed, and concord is what follows.

Use the root in a new word: accordion

Use the root in a new word: accordion: The accordion is named for its chords — notes sounding in agreement as the bellows squeeze.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / diplomatic

Accord is the diplomat's word for the signed agreement itself. A treaty is the heavier legal instrument between nations; a pact is tighter and sometimes secret. Concord, its cousin in this unit, names the state of harmony that follows — you sign an accord and then live in concord.
